chapter: Claude Hopkins, Fletcher Henderson and Fats Waller
title: Roseland with Hopkins and the story of Orlando Roberson
summary: A season at Roseland, a funny North Carolina incident with Orlando Roberson, and Hopkins's jealousy of him.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When you were here in New York were you in Roseland with Claude?
Oh yeah. You see, I went in Roseland--we
played about--
It must be in the fall.
It was fall.
It must have been a whole season.
I did.
That was a nice job.
That was a fine job.
You had all those (inaudible)
Orlando Roberson.
Yeah, Orlando. What was that story--where were you playing when Claude came into town?

That was the funniest thing, that was down in North Carolina. We got in town early in the morning in the bus and there was a great big--they used to advertise the dances on these wagons, with a sign on each side, and there was Orlando Roberson. Boy, I never heard so many so and so's. You could hardly blame him really.
Was he hard to get along with?
No. To tell the truth, Claude was jealous of Orlando.
I guess so.
On my radio show, a month or a month and a half ago, I played--I've got the record over there of Orlando singing 'Trees'; I've got the record.
My wife loves that, she's crazy about that.
Do you want to make a tape on it?
I think I have it at home. I did get a copy finally.
And 'Love in Bloom;' have you got that?
I don't know.
I've got a record of Orlando singing that.
Was he singing 'Trees' when you were in the band?
